en.title: Minimum Deletions So a Center Interval Touches Every Remaining Merchant
en.description:
Each merchant corresponds to a closed interval. Delete the fewest merchants so that the remaining merchants include a center merchant whose interval intersects the interval of every other remaining merchant. Sharing an endpoint counts as intersecting. All intervals do not need a common point, and it is not enough for them to be connected as a whole.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n, followed by n lines of start end. The original bounds are 1≤n≤100000, 1≤start≤end≤10^9, and duplicate intervals are allowed.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The answers are 2, 0 and 2. In the first example the center [3,8] touches two disjoint small intervals at once, so the maximum simultaneous coverage cannot be used instead.
hints: Sort all starts and all ends separately. The number of merchants a center [l,r] can keep is the number of starts ≤r minus the number of ends <l; maximize this count and subtract it from n.
